findings.reason: The authentic standalone original tile renders the formulas correctly but has no illustration. A concrete same-scale interval diagram materially clarifies why two disjoint quarter intervals map onto one half interval while that half interval maps forward onto the whole circle. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram criterion, not a claim that the existing proof was incomplete.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ interval schematic in final Remarks, with two branches over A, a separate forward-image pair for B, explicit endpoint conventions, and independence from the verification.

correction: Appended only Remarks and a TikZ diagram showing D^{-1}(A)=[0,1/4) union [1/2,3/4), A=[0,1/2), B=[0,1/2), and D(B)=[0,1), with branch labels 2x and 2x-1.

diagram_math_checks.objects_and_domains: The circle is represented by [0,1), as in def-circle-rotation-and-doubling-map. A and B both denote [0,1/2); their distinct letters distinguish target and source roles in the two panels. All four rows have the same horizontal scale.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The item Example and Verification 1.1–2.1, together with the supplier definition of D(x)={2x}.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The first highlighted component [0,1/4) maps onto A by x -> 2x; the second [1/2,3/4) maps onto A by x -> 2x-1. The two downward arrows indicate maps between intervals, rather than trajectories of their drawn attachment points.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 1.1 explicitly solves 0<=2x<1/2 and 0<=2x-1<1/2 on the exhaustive two branches. Each component has length 1/4, so the drawn union has length 1/2.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Filled endpoints at 0 and 1/2 in the preimage row are included and map to 0. Hollow endpoints at 1/4 and 3/4 are excluded and map to 1/2, the hollow endpoint of A.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 2.1 explicitly identifies these endpoints and their images; the diagram preserves the half-open intervals of the Example.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The lower arrow is the restriction D:B -> [0,1), x -> 2x. B has length 1/2 and D(B) has length one; 0 is included and the right endpoints 1/2 and 1 are excluded.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 2.1 gives x=y/2 for every y in [0,1), proving surjectivity of this restriction. This displays forward-image expansion without contradicting inverse-image preservation.

diagram_math_checks.proof_independence: The full original Example, Facts and Verification are byte-preserved. The Remarks explicitly state that the verification is independent of the picture.
